In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live.

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release.

Industry observers note that in a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and showed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'.

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The newly introduced boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Recent findings suggest that alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the initiative.'.

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

It has been revealed that 'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'.

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9.

Conor McGregor confirmed that he would give employees at various businesses the day off.

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern.

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the new GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

He told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'.

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the newly introduced game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor declared that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was launched.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously stated: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'.

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the strategy.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game.

Industry observers note that 'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, remarked with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a big one.'.

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

In a recent development, 'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' said Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'.

It has been revealed that latest York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall remarked. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'.

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

Industry observers note that A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'.

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after big games.

Those problems appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony said it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event.

Department store chain John Lewis noted it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

In a recent development, I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Bournemouth manager Marco Rose has mentioned the club do not plan to sell Arsenal and Tottenham target Eli Junior Kroupi in January.

Both north London clubs have been heavily linked with a move for the French striker, who scored his first senior goal against Turkey last weekend, during the summer before he suffered a foot injury in pre-season which required surgery.

Kroupi has recently returned to fitness after more than four months out, stoking speculation that goal-shy Spurs could reignite their interest in the 20-year-old, who scored more goals than any other teenager in their debut Premier League season last term.

In an interview with The Times, though, Rose has revealed that Bournemouth do not plan on selling any of their star talent in January.

That also includes midfielder Alex Scott, who was the subject of two rejected bids from Chelsea over the summer and is also stated to be attracting interest from Liverpool and Premier League champions Arsenal.

“It’s not the plan to sell someone in January,” Rose stated, though he later admitted selling players was “part of the process” for Bournemouth as they look to comply with UEFA’s squad cost rules.

“It’s not our blueprint and so far there are just rumours and noises. We are quite calm, like we were in the summer and I think everything we said was clear and the things happened the way we communicated. For us, it’s not a plan to sell someone in January.”.

After failing to win any of their first six league games, the Cherries have hit form under Rose and have won each of their last eight games in all competitions.

There were question marks early on about whether Rose could handle the step up to the Premier League.

But the highly-rated German has now firmly dismissed those suggestions, with the Dorset club sitting sit joint-second in the form table across Europe’s five major leagues, behind only Paris Saint-Germain and level with Real Madrid.

Bournemouth appear to have made a shrewd appointment in naming Rose as Andoni Iraola’s successor, but he admits it all could have been very different, with Spurs sounding him out to take over as interim manager before landing on the ill-fated appointment of Igor Tudor.

No concrete offer was made by the north Londoners, but Rose indicates there was interest from the capital and a number of other Premier League teams.

“No, they didn’t make me an offer,” Rose added.

“I was in touch with some Premier League clubs, that’s right, but it was never to speak about a real offer. I did it the same way as with Bournemouth, I tried to get to know the environment, the club, the situation and then I picked the club I felt could be the right next step for me. The other club decided to take another manager, so it’s not always just about me.”.

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 14:35, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:09.

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly interested in signing Inter Milan midfielder Hakan Calhanoglu.

After enjoying a memorable spell at AC Milan, Calhanoglu switched to their cross-city rivals Inter in the summer of 2021 and has since made 225 appearances across all competitions.

The highly-skilled central midfielder has scored 53 goals and registered 39 assists for Inter, while continuing to impress with his performances this season.

However, his contract situation has cast doubt over his long-term future at the club, with several sides, including Tottenham, reportedly looking to take advantage of the uncertainty.

The Turkish international has a contract at San Siro until 2027, but he is yet to receive an offer to extend his stay.

The 32-year-old wants to continue with Inter, although doing so could require him to accept a significant pay cut, something he is currently unwilling to consider.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb, Tottenham are ready to welcome the midfielder, but face competition from Galatasaray, Juventus and Como.

Spurs spent heavily during the summer transfer window to overhaul their midfield, bringing in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes on big-money deals.

After a nightmare start to the season, Roberto De Zerbi's side are gradually climbing the table and currently sit 11th in the Premier League table with 12 points from 10 matches.

De Zerbi already has plenty of midfield options at his disposal, but it appears he wants a technically gifted and versatile player with proven experience, making Calhanoglu an attractive option.

Calhanoglu operates primarily as a defensive midfielder, although his creative qualities remain a significant asset.

Furthermore, the former Bayer Leverkusen midfielder is renowned for his excellent long-range shooting and could adapt well to the Premier League, even at this stage of his career.

Alan Shearer is back with his latest predictions as Premier League action resumes after the international break.

The Red Devils are winless in their last eight games, but will hope that their latest head coach can inspire them to a famous win against their arch-rivals Liverpool.

Elsewhere, Chelsea and Manchester City will look to get back to winning ways after defeats before the international break, while Thomas Frank begins life at Crystal Palace with a trip to Coventry.

As ever, England legend and Betfair ambassador Alan Shearer has revealed his Premier League predictions to Metro.

I think City will get back on track here. I know it’s sometimes difficult after international breaks, but I saw Fulham against Newcastle and they deserved the point. But I think City will be too strong for them to get back to winning ways, and they need to get back to winning ways here.

Alan’s Prediction: Man City Win.

Recent findings suggest that I don’t think Sunderland will get a result. I think Villa will have too much for them. I think Sunderland will struggle, you can see that they are clearly finding it difficult with European football.

Industry observers note that they’ve a couple of injuries, when Brian Brobbey is not in the team, clearly, they’re not as potent. So, I think Villa will have too much for them on Saturday.

Alan’s Prediction: Aston Villa Win.

Recent findings suggest that this is a tough one to call. Forest will take big confidence from that performance before the international break against Man City, and deservedly so, the two goals from Liam Delap were brilliant and he can take confidence from those strikes as well.

According to recent reports, this is a Difficult one to call it because Bournemouth are flying. Forest got a great result. I’m just going to go for Bournemouth just because of home advantage, but I think Forest will make it tough for them after that win against City.

Alan’s Prediction: Bournemouth Win.

I think Leeds will make it tough for Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. They know that they’ve not got the speed with Joao Pedro, and I don’t think they’re great defensively. I think it’ll be a very up and down season for Chelsea.

Industry observers note that this is a huge game. It could have huge ramifications even so early in the season. Already you could feel as if this is a big, big game for relegation candidates.

It is also a big one for Thomas Frank to go into. Frank Lampard will know the same, and being at home, he’ll be expected to get something out of the game. I’m going to go for an away win, though.

Spurs are another team that need their centre-forward to start scoring goals, but I still think they’ll have enough for Ipswich at the weekend.

Alan’s Prediction: Tottenham Win.

Industry observers note that this is a tough one to predict. I’d love to see Newcastle win, but that would be my heart ruling my head. I think it’s a tough game because of the way Arsenal are playing at this moment in time, and the way Newcastle are. I have to say an away win.

According to recent reports, brighton have been sensational and the more wins they tick off, the more people are going to have to take them seriously. They’ve beaten City and they’ve beaten Arsenal. So, I do expect them to go to Hull and win.

Alan’s Prediction: Brighton Win.

Sources indicate that I think Liverpool will win it. It depends on Mauricio Pochettino, though. Is he going to have enough time to actually get his ideas and his beliefs and his thoughts across?

I think he will eventually, but it will take longer than people think, and for that reason, I’ve got no faith defensively in Manchester United, and I think Liverpool will be too strong for them in both departments.

Alan’s Prediction: Liverpool Win.

I think it’ll be a draw. I think defensively Everton might be tough to break down. They’ll set up tough to frustrate Brentford. Brentford are not in great form at the moment and could do with a massive result. However, I’m going to stay on the fence and say a point each on this one.

Mauricio Pochettino has already been bending Premier League rules just days into his tenure as Manchester United manager.

It has been a whirlwind start to life at Man Utd for Pochettino, who flew into the club’s training ground in Manchester on Wednesday, took charge of his first training session on Thursday - which was inadvertently overseen by a drone - and will conduct his first press conference on Friday.

Luckily, though, the Premier League have lent a a helping hand.

Under league rules, Friday press conferences must take place by 1.30pm at the latest.

However, according to Manchester Evening News, Pochettino has been given permission to start his at 2pm because of the unusual circumstances surrounding his arrival.

The Argentine will speak to the assembled media later than any other manager to discuss his first game in charge, which is a daunting trip to face Liverpool at Anfield.

It will be Pochettino’s second game inside five games, having overseen the United States national team beating Haiti on Tuesday.

But the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager is not running on fumes just yet.

“I have plenty of energy,” he said this week. “It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United. And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

The Argentine spoke to the media on Friday afternoon at his press conference ahead of Sunday's Premier League contest with Liverpool.

Pochettino was asked about low confidence in the camp, with Man United having an incredibly difficult campaign to date.

TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 103 min read (20572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~103 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A major goal in neuroscience is to map the transformation of information as it flows through the brain.
  • In a recent development, A central objective in neuroscience is to characterize the computational transformations that occur across successive nodes of neural circuits.
  • Efforts to map neural circuits have yielded a diverse array of methodologies, yet existing ‘gold-standard’ approaches face considerable scalability and molecular identification constraints.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A major goal in neuroscience is to map the transformation of information as it flows through the brain. For example, neurons at many levels of the visual hierarchy are attuned to motion direction1,2,3,4,5. However, links between motion-selective computations and cell types at various stages of the visual hierarchy remain unidentified. A key first step in delineating these relationships is to map the wiring diagrams that connect different motion-selective cell types. Here we establish a systematic, cell-type-specific circuit-mapping method, combining an anterograde trans-neuronal fluorescent tracer (mWGA–mCherry)6 with spatial transcriptomics (multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH))7,8 to establish TransA-MERFISH. We used TransA-MERFISH to comprehensively map the synaptic target cell types of four retinal ganglion cell subclasses in superior colliculus (SC) at cell-type resolution. These experiments unexpectedly revealed that retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cells (ooDSGCs) innervate several direction-selective SC cell types, but do not innervate a SC cell type that was previously reported to display strong direction-selective responses. We validated these results using orthogonal approaches and demonstrated the sensitivity and specificity of TransA-MERFISH. Functional studies of SC activity before and after ablation of retinal direction-selective circuits confirmed that these computationally distinct, ooDSGC-dependent and -independent direction-selective cell types are commingled in SC. Together, our study establishes TransA-MERFISH as a robust framework for mapping wiring diagrams at the cell-type level and uncovers divergent computational mechanisms of motion detection in early visual processing.

In a recent development, A central objective in neuroscience is to characterize the computational transformations that occur across successive nodes of neural circuits. In the visual system, this requires defining the mechanisms by which retinal signals are integrated and processed as they ascend to higher brain centres. Among these, motion signals are particularly salient, providing the sensory substrate for critical behaviours such as predatory pursuit, escape and spatial navigation9,10. Over the past half-century, neurons in various brain areas have been found to respond to visual motion. A particularly common form of motion sensitivity is a preference for stimuli moving in a certain direction, a property known as direction selectivity that is observed in the retina, SC and cortex1,2,3,4,5. However, relationships between direction-selective cell types in different brain areas are unknown, leaving equally unclear how direction-selective activity is used and transformed across different stages of the visual hierarchy. A key obstacle has been the lack of a wiring diagram to guide understanding of information flow between the tens of different retinal ganglion cell (RGC) types and similarly diverse neuronal cell types in target areas such as SC. Here, we describe the development of a technological platform that enabled us to address these knowledge gaps.

Efforts to map neural circuits have yielded a diverse array of methodologies, yet existing ‘gold-standard’ approaches face considerable scalability and molecular identification constraints. Although electron microscopy provides high-resolution reconstructions11,12,13,14, it remains incompatible with the molecular profiling of pre- and postsynaptic partners and is at the moment impractical for brain-wide mammalian applications. Similarly, physiological techniques such as channelrhodopsin-assisted circuit mapping (CRACM)12 and Patch-seq15,16 provide precise functional data but are limited by low throughput. Recent sequencing-based strategies (such as Retro-Seq, Project-Seq, VECTOR-Seq, MAPseq and BARseq)17,18,19,20,21 have advanced the field by using RNA barcodes to define projection targets of starter neurons at high throughput, but these strategies trace axonal projection targets in the brain, and do not identify their synaptic target cell types within those areas. Additionally, these methods often rely on tissue microdissection, thereby losing anatomical context. These limitations underscore the need for next-generation, readily adoptable methods for comprehensive connectivity mapping at cell-type resolution.

Sources indicate that to fill this gap, with a particular focus on comprehensive mapping of synaptic target cell types, we integrated a genetically encoded anterograde fluorescent trans-neuronal tracer, mWGA–mCherry (mWmC)6, (Fig. 1a) with the spatial transcriptomics technology, MERFISH7,8 (Fig. 1b). This combined platform, which we named TransA-MERFISH, required two major technical advances. First, we established an experimental workflow that enables the combination of anterograde trans-neuronal tracer immunostaining and MERFISH-based spatial transcriptomics. Second, we developed an automated data processing pipeline to align connectivity and transcriptomic data—that is, to overlay fluorescent signals from anterograde tracers on the spatially resolved neural identity data derived from multiplexed RNA signals in MERFISH (Fig. 1c). We then applied TransA-MERFISH to investigate the aforementioned half-century-old unresolved problem in visual neuroscience: the relationship between direction-selective neuron types and computations at different stages of the visual hierarchy. We used TransA-MERFISH to establish a comprehensive, cell-type-resolution wiring diagram downstream of ooDSGCs, a well-studied RGC subclass attuned to stimuli moving in one of the four cardinal directions: nasal, temporal, dorsal or ventral22,23. Using Cre transgenic mice, we mapped the SC synaptic target cell types of ooDSGCs that prefer particular directions24,25,26. We unexpectedly found that although ooDSGCs strongly innervate several SC cell types, they do not innervate the cell type that a previous study27 claimed was most direction-selective in SC. These surprising results were validated using multiple genetic, anatomical and electrophysiological tests. Subsequent in vivo imaging studies of SC activity before and after ablation of retinal direction-selective circuits confirmed that computationally distinct ooDSGC-dependent and ooDSGC-independent direction-selective cell types are commingled in SC. Our research establishes TransA-MERFISH as a high-throughput approach for generating cell-type-level wiring diagrams and reveals divergent computational strategies for visual motion detection.

Anti-RFP immunostaining was used for mWmC+ cell identification in the MERFISH-segmented atlas. d,e, Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) plot classifying sSC neurons into 8 ENCs and 11 INCs (d) and with superimposed Slc17a6 (excitatory neurons) and Gad1 (inhibitory neurons) expression (e). f, Median positions of somata along the dorsal–ventral axis for all clusters. It has been revealed that single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq)-based methods have laid the groundwork for understanding neuronal taxonomy, including scRNA-seq studies covering the entire SC region28,29. However, these methods require tissue dissociation and microfluidics-based single-cell isolation, which reduce spatial resolution, the completeness of cell-type identification, and scalability for large-scale mapping. We therefore developed a preparation to combine anterograde trans-neuronal tracing with spatial transcriptomics (MERFISH). Because the established MERFISH protocol uses fresh-frozen tissue to maximize RNA preservation30,31, it is incompatible with immunostaining for protein markers such as the anterograde trans-neuronal tracer mWmC. Therefore, we developed a protocol to perform MERFISH on fixed tissue. To benchmark this protocol, we sought to create a reference atlas of SC neurons in the retino-recipient superficial SC (sSC) (Fig. 1c). We referred to existing scRNA-seq data6,19,28 to select 140 neuron-type marker genes to classify retino-recipient neurons in the superficial SC (sSC) (Fig. 1b, Extended Data Figs. 1e,f and 2f,i and Methods). We developed a perfusion–fixation MERFISH protocol that ensured that RNA integrity and neuronal morphology were not compromised compared with fresh-frozen tissue, while preserving protein localization (Extended Data Fig. 1a–d and Methods). We then performed MERFISH on sSC, followed by Cellpose-based segmentation (as in past MERFISH studies in the mouse brain31), which covered all sSC neurons (Fig. 1h,i and Methods). This pipeline classified sSC neurons into 8 excitatory cell types (ENC1–8, marked by Slc17a6) and 11 inhibitory cell types (INC1–11, marked by Gad1) (Fig. 1d–g and Extended Data Fig. 1g–j). Data quality for SC cell classification from the modified TransA-MERFISH protocol (Extended Data Fig. 3a–e) closely matched that of several published scRNA-seq datasets19,27,28 (Extended Data Fig. 2c,e–j), as well as the cell types and supertypes reported in the Allen Brain Atlas dataset30 (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b). Together, these data validate the feasibility of performing MERFISH in fixed tissue.

Analysis of spatial distributions found that each ENC cluster is restricted to a specific sublamina along the dorsal–ventral axis (Fig. 1f and Extended Data Fig. 4f), consistent with past observations in rodents and zebrafish6,32,33,34. INC1, INC2, INC5 and INC6 are also restricted to specific sublaminae along the dorsal–ventral axis, whereas INC3, INC4 and INC7–11 are spread across multiple sublaminae (Fig. 1f and Extended Data Fig. 4g). In addition, we observed a consistent distribution of all ENCs and INCs along the anterior–posterior and medial–lateral axes, which largely follows the sublaminar arrangement, without layer swapping (Extended Data Fig. 4a–e). Collectively, the MERFISH data map the sublaminar distribution of sSC neurons along the dorsal–ventral axis at single-cell-type resolution. Each cluster is further compared and quantified in Extended Data Table 1.

Having established a MERFISH protocol compatible with immunostaining and created an atlas of sSC cell types, we next sought to overlay cell connectivity information onto it. To do so, adeno-associated virus (AAV) encoding mWmC was delivered to the left eye to yield nearly complete coverage across all RGC types (Fig. 1a and Extended Data Fig. 6a). mWmC protein was transferred anterogradely and monosynaptically to the synaptic targets of RGCs in the contralateral (right) sSC, which receives innervation from around 90% of RGCs35. We then performed MERFISH on fixed tissue followed by anti-RFP immunostaining on the same microscope to facilitate registration with the MERFISH data. As a result, mWmC signals identified by anti-RFP immunostaining could be clearly registered with the RNA-based Cellpose segmentation masks (Fig. 1i,j and Methods). All mWmC+ neurons in the SC downstream of a given RGC starter neuron could be captured by imaging approaches and molecularly identified using MERFISH. Based on co-registered mWmC signals and MERFISH transcripts, we established a computational pipeline to assign mWmC signals to segmented neurons at single-cell resolution, followed by manual proofreading (Fig. 1i,j and Methods). The optimized workflow enabled high-throughput registration. This computational pipeline determines the percentages of mWmC+ neurons within each neuronal cluster, providing a quantitative measure of connectivity at cell-type resolution (Fig. 1k and Methods). We termed this integrated workflow TransA-MERFISH because it combines anterograde trans-neuronal tracing with MERFISH-based cell classification to read out connectivity.

Using TransA-MERFISH, we examined the synaptic target cell types of all RGCs. Roughly half (49 ± 3%, mean ± s.e.m.) of sSC neurons had a detectable mWmC signal (Fig. 1k). Across sSC neuron types defined by MERFISH, 5 out of 8 ENCs and 6 out of 11 INCs were classified as retino-recipient neurons based on mWmC signals above baseline, including a cell type that we recently showed to be retino-recipient (Npnt+)6 (Figs. 1k and 2a,c and Extended Data Fig. 3f–h). Notably, multiple ENCs and INCs in the sSC did not receive mWmC and were therefore not categorized as recipient neurons of RGCs, including a cell type that was previously6 characterized as not retino-recipient (Etv1+) (Figs. 1k and 2c,o). These data thus suggest TransA-MERFISH possesses the sensitivity and specificity to map synaptic connectivity at scale.

According to recent reports, the spatially resolved map of all retino-recipient neurons in SC (Fig. 2b) generated with TransA-MERFISh enabled direct comparison of connectivity across cell types within shared sublaminar contexts. Notably, several SC neuron pairs exhibited divergent RGC connectivity despite occupying similar sublaminar distributions (Figs. 1f and 2a,b,g–o). For example, in the most superficial SC, ENC1 and ENC2 neurons were retino-recipient, whereas neighbouring INC1 neurons were not; similarly, in slightly deeper layers, ENC5 and INC6 neurons received retinal input, whereas neighbouring ENC6 neurons did not. These observations suggested that sublaminar position alone is insufficient to explain synaptic targeting by RGC axons. To test whether molecular cell-type identity contributes to synaptic specificity beyond sublaminar organization, we implemented a permutation-based framework in which cell-type labels were randomly shuffled within depth bins along the dorsal–ventral axis (Fig. 2d and Methods). This procedure preserves the sublaminar distribution of mWmC labelling while disrupting the association between molecular identity and connectivity. Cell-type specificity was quantified by comparing observed mWmC enrichment or depletion for each cell type against the permutation-derived null distribution. Using this approach, we identified multiple retino-recipient clusters, including ENC1, ENC2 and ENC5, with significant enrichment of mWmC labelling after accounting for sublaminar positions (Fig. 2e). By contrast, multiple non-retino-recipient clusters, including INC1 and ENC6, characterized here, showed significant depletion relative to sublaminar expectations (Fig. 2e,p). Together, these results indicate that RGC axons innervate SC neurons in a cell-type-specific way rather than simply according to their sublaminar distributions; that is, molecular identity, rather than sublaminar distribution, determines wiring specificity from the retina to SC.

According to recent reports, we validated the sensitivity and specificity of TransA-MERFISH using CRACM. We first examined ENC5, which corresponds to genetically labelled Npnt+ wide-field neurons6 (Extended Data Fig. 5i and Extended Data Table 1). ENC5 was known to receive strong RGC input: 54 ± 6% (mean ± s.e.m.) of Npnt+ neurons contained mWmC labelling (Fig. 1j,k). CRACM quantitatively validated the TransA-MERFISH prediction, with a comparable percentage (52 ± 2%, mean ± s.e.m.) of Npnt+ wide-field neurons innervated by RGCs (Extended Data Fig. 5a,b,d). By contrast, ENC6 neurons, marked by Etv1, were in the same sublamina as ENC5 but did not receive direct retinal input in the TransA-MERFISH data (Fig. 1k). Consistently, these neurons did not receive RGC input in CRACM experiments (Extended Data Fig. 5a,c,d). These results validated the finding that ENC5 neurons receive input from the retina, whereas ENC6 neurons are not innervated by RGCs (Extended Data Fig. 5e–h). Together, these data support the notion that TransA-MERFISH provides a high-throughput platform for quantitatively defining neuronal synaptic target cell types at cell-type resolution.

Industry observers note that to demonstrate the power of TransA-MERFISH to enable the discovery of synaptic target cell types of genetically defined starter cells, we decoded synaptic target cell types in SC of four major RGC subclasses that detect distinct visual features36: αRGCs (Kcng4-cre); ooDSGCs (Cartpt-cre); F-RGCs (Foxp2-cre); and T5-RGCs (Tusc5-cre)24,37,38,39,40 (Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 6). These parallel TransA-MERFISH experiments yielded a comprehensive connectivity matrix at cell-type resolution. We observed highly distinct synaptic target cell-type compositions for different RGC subclasses (Fig. 2g–n). For example, ENC5 (Npnt+) neurons receive input from αRGCs, but not from ooDSGCs, consistent with our CRACM and trans-neuronal tracing results, and ENC6 (Etv1+) neurons receive no input from any of the four RGC subclasses (Figs. 1k, 2f–n,p and Extended Data Fig. 7). In addition, because different RGC subclasses arborize in distinct sSC sublaminae, we sorted the synaptic target cell types by their sublaminar distributions and connectivity frequencies (Fig. 2b,h,j,l,n and Extended Data Fig. 7). We found that retino-recipient neurons largely share the sublaminar distributions of the axonal arbors from that RGC subclass. For example, robust connectivity was reported from αRGCs to ENC4 and ENC5 neurons in lower stratum griseum superficiale (SGS) and stratum opticum (SO) (Fig. 2g,h and Extended Data Fig. 7b), with αRGC axons primarily ramifying in the same sublaminae24,26,40,41 (Extended Data Fig. 6i). By contrast, ooDSGCs, F-RGCs and T5-RGCs primarily innervated superficial ENC1 and ENC2 (Fig. 2i–n and Extended Data Fig. 7b–f), correlated with their axons primarily innervating the upper SGS (Extended Data Fig. 6i). Collectively, the TransA-MERFISH data provided a detailed neuronal connectivity map from the retina to SC at the level of cell types, offering functional insights into parallel retinotectal circuit organization and further validating the sensitivity and specificity of this tool for mapping comprehensive connectomes in a high-throughput manner.

It has been revealed that A notable finding emerged from analysis of the synaptic target cell types of Cartpt-cre-labelled RGCs, which are ooDSGCs that are reported to prefer upward (dorsal) or downward (ventral) motion24,42. Cartpt+ ooDSGCs innervated 3 ENC clusters (ENC1, ENC2 and ENC4) as well as 4 INC clusters (INC3, INC4, INC5 and INC9) (Figs. 2i,j and 3c). The strongest targets of ooDSGCs, ENC1 and ENC2, are excitatory clusters marked by Cdh7 (Figs. 1g and 3a–d and Extended Data Fig. 2d). They are in the most superficial 100 µm of SGS, commingled with INC1 neurons, which are marked by Cbln4 (Fig. 1g) and are negative for mWmC labelling (Fig. 3c,d). Notably, the permutation test on TransA-MERFISH data (Fig. 2d,e) also showed that ENC1 and ENC2 have the highest synaptic enrichment for innervation from the retina, whereas INC1 neurons have the lowest (Fig. 2e), emphasizing the importance of cell-type-specific molecular properties among these neuron clusters in recruiting ooDSGC input.

The lack of mWmC labelling from ooDSGCs in INC1 was unexpected, because a recent study combining calcium imaging with post hoc in situ hybridization found that Cbln4+ SC neurons were strongly direction-selective31. Moreover, other studies have suggested that SC direction selectivity depends on ooDSGCs43,44. Together, these results appear to predict that the strongly direction-selective Cbln4+ SC neurons would be innervated by ooDSGCs. Therefore, to verify these findings, we generated the FlpO knock-in lines Cdh7-FlpO (Fig. 3e–h, Extended Data Fig. 5j,k,p,q and Methods) and Cbln4-FlpO (Fig. 3i–l, Extended Data Fig. 5l–o and Methods), and performed CRACM, mWmC anterograde tracing and rabies retrograde tracing. All of these methods confirmed strong monosynaptic input from ooDSGCs to Cdh7+ SC neurons (Fig. 3m,n,r,s and Extended Data Fig. 8a–c,h,j,l) but not from ooDSGCs to Cbln4+ SC neurons (Fig. 3m,o,r,t and Extended Data Fig. 8d,e,i,j,m). Moreover, mWmC anterograde and rabies retrograde tracing found negligible input from RGCs in either the contralateral or ipsilateral eye to Cbln4+ SC neurons, and CRACM using all RGC expression of ChR2 did not detect monosynaptic input from contralateral RGCs to Cbln4+ SC neurons, consistent with the TransA-MERFISH data (Figs. 2a and 3p,q,u and Extended Data Fig. 8f,g,k,n,o). These experiments thus validate the unexpected finding from TransA-MERFISH that the strongly direction-selective Cbln4+ SC neurons are not innervated by ooDSGCs from either the contralateral or ipsilateral eye (Figs. 2f,i,j and 3q and Extended Data Fig. 8d,e,k,o). These results demonstrate the specificity and sensitivity of TransA-MERFISH for systematic synaptic target cell-type mapping, enabling biological discovery.

Recent findings suggest that the preceding circuit tracing data suggested that Cdh7+ SC neurons may inherit their direction selectivity from ooDSGCs, whereas Cbln4+ SC neurons may not. A key functional prediction of this differential wiring is that the direction selectivity of Cdh7+ SC neurons depends on the retinal ooDSGC circuit, whereas that of Cbln4+ SC neurons does not. To test this prediction, we used two-photon calcium imaging (Fig. 4a,d,i,l) to analyse the direction selectivity of both SC cell types at baseline and after ablation of starburst amacrine cells (SACs), which reduces direction selectivity of ooDSGCs45 (Fig. 4b,c,j,k,q,r and Extended Data Fig. 9a–f). Consistent with predictions from our TransA-MERFISH experiments, SAC ablation reduced the direction selectivity of Cdh7+ SC neurons (Fig. 4c,f–h) but not of Cbln4+ SC neurons (Fig. 4k,n–p). We further examined the contribution of ipsilateral retinal ooDSGCs by covering the ipsilateral eye and ablating SACs bilaterally (Extended Data Fig. 9m,o) and found no changes in direction selectivity in Cbln4+ SC neurons (Extended Data Fig. 9n,p). These data indicate that the direction selectivity of Cbln4+ SC neurons is independent of retinal ooDSGCs, whereas Cdh7+ SC neurons inherit direction selectivity from retinal ooDSGCs. Together, these data support the notion that multiple mechanisms underlie computationally distinct direction selectivity across different SC neuron types, including retinal ooDSGC-dependent direction selectivity in Cdh7+ SC neurons and retinal ooDSGC-independent direction selectivity in Cbln4+ SC neurons. Analysis of the preferred directions of these two populations revealed another marked difference: in the imaged region of SC (posterior and medial), Cdh7+ SC neurons showed a broad distribution in preferred directions (Fig. 4q and Extended Data Fig. 9g–i), whereas Cbln4+ SC neurons preferred a very narrow distribution of direction, mainly preferring dorsal-to-nasal motion (Fig. 4r and Extended Data Fig. 9j–l). These differential population biases suggest that these neurons are likely to participate in distinct circuits (Fig. 4s).
