a, Unsupervised classification of sSC using the standard fresh-frozen MERFISH protocol. UMAP embedding of 5,845 cells reveals consistent clustering of the same 8 ENCs and 11 INCs identified with TransA-MERFISH on fixed tissue (Fig. 1d). Cell-type labels were assigned to Leiden clusters based on canonical marker gene expression patterns and transcriptomic mapping via a supervised XGBoost classifier trained on the TransA-MERFISH atlas. b, Confusion matrix showing transcriptomic correspondence between cell types in standard MERFISH (rows) and TransA-MERFISH (columns). c, Violin plots comparing quality control metrics between standard MERFISH (blue) and TransA-MERFISH (gray). Distributions are highly similar across key metrics, including the number of genes detected per cell (n_genes_by_counts), total transcript counts per cell (total_counts), and cell mask area (in pixels). A modest reduction in n_genes_by_counts and total_counts was observed in TransA-MERFISH experiments. d, Comparison of matched neuronal subtype frequencies between standard MERFISH and TransA-MERFISH. Values are plotted on a ln-ln scale to highlight low-frequency types. A strong correlation is observed across both excitatory and inhibitory populations, indicating that the TransA-MERFISH protocol did not bias or deplete neuron types in the sSC (Pearson R = 0.88). e, Validation accuracies of the XGBoost classifier trained using various gene selection strategies: the performance of the 140-gene TransA-MERFISH panel was compared to randomly sampled 140-gene sets drawn from either the full single-cell transcriptome or the top 2000 highly variable genes (HVGs). Additional gene sets were constructed by selecting the top k specific genes (Methods) per SC neuronal cluster (k = 1–10), based on 19 neuronal clusters identified from re-clustering of the neuronal subset of the dataset28. Data are presented as mean ± SD. f, Dot plots comparing the expression patterns of 2 non-optimal probes (top row, blue) with their corresponding expressions in snRNA-seq17 (bottom row, orange). MERFISH cells are grouped according to their predicted snRNA-seq cluster identities, as inferred by Tangram-based imputation (Methods). The 140-gene list is presented in Supplementary Table 1. g-j, Classification and filtering of non-neuron cells (NNs). UMAP embedding (g) of all high-quality cells (47740 cells after quality filtering, see Methods) before filtering out non-neuronal cells, colored by broad cell classes: excitatory neurons (ENCs), inhibitory neurons (INCs), and NNs. NNs were identified using a supervised XGBoost classifier (i) trained on an SC snRNA-seq dataset, as in the reference28. Violin plots (h) of quality control metrics show that NNs exhibit reduced numbers of detected genes per cell (n_genes_by_counts) and total transcripts per cell (total_counts), consistent with the design principles for neurons in the TransA-MERFISH gene panel. Bar plots (j) showing the average proportions of ENCs and INCs among all detected cells across animals. NNs were subsequently filtered out before re-clustering of neuronal cells to improve classification resolution among neuronal types. n = 16 animals. Data are presented as mean ± s.e.m.

a,b, Transcriptomic correspondence between the MERFISH-based sSC neuron atlas and the 10x Genomics-based Whole Mouse Brain (WMB) taxonomy (CCN20230722; Allen Institute)20. (a) UMAP embedding of the TransA-MERFISH neuron atlas (Fig. 1d), colored by the most probable mapped supertype identity inferred via MapMyCells. (b) Confusion matrix showing the correspondence between TransA-MERFISH neuronal types (rows) and 10 x WMB supertypes (columns), as determined by MapMyCells mapping (Methods). c, Transcriptomic correspondence between the TransA-MERFISH sSC neuron atlas and the Trans-Seq single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) SC neuron atlas9, as determined by XGBoost-based classification (Methods). Dot size and color represent the proportion of cells from each Trans-Seq cluster (y-axis) mapped to the corresponding TransA-MERFISH neuronal types (x-axis), indicating the scRNA-seq-based protocol biases a few neuronal subsets due to the nature of the dissociation and FACS sorting, thus it is not optimal to represent adult neuron clusters precisely and comprehensively. d, Dot plot comparing transcriptomic signatures of representative neuronal types across three datasets: TransA-MERFISH (red), single-nucleus RNA-seq (green)22, and supertypes from the 10x Genomics-based Whole Mouse Brain (WMB) taxonomy (blue; corresponding to panels a,b). Shown are selected excitatory neuron types—including Cdh7+ SC neurons (ENC1, ENC2), Npnt+ wide-field SC neurons (ENC5), and Etv1+ SC neurons (ENC6)—as well as inhibitory neuron types, including Cbln4+ SC neurons (INC1) and Fibcd1+ SC neurons (INC3). The consistent expression patterns of key marker genes across datasets support the robustness of cell classification in the TransA-MERFISH atlas and align with mapping results obtained via machine learning (g,j) and MapMyCells (a,b). e-j, Alignments of the TransA-MERFISH neuronal clusters with past single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-Seq) atlases of the mouse SC, indicating consistency across datasets. Re-clustering of neuronal subsets from reference datasets reproduced the original cell-type assignments (e17 and h22). Confusion matrices (f,i) show that XGBoost models trained on the 140-gene TransA-MERFISH panel achieve high validation accuracy in recovering snRNA-seq-defined cell types. Heatmaps (g,j) show the transcriptomic correspondence between snRNA-seq cell clusters (y-axis) and the TransA-MERFISH types (x-axis), based on predictions from an XGBoost classifier trained on the TransA-MERFISH dataset using the 140 genes. Color intensity reflects the percentage of cells from each snRNA-seq cluster mapped to each TransA-MERFISH type.

a-b, UMAP embedding of TransA-MERFISH neuron atlas (Fig. 1d), with cells colored by individual dataset identities corresponding to each reaction (a), and split UMAP embedding for each replicate separately (b), showing consistent cluster structure across replicates. c, Histograms display consistent percentages of neurons for each dataset contributing to each identified neuron type, for a stable representation of cell types across datasets. d, Violin plots showing the distributions of the number of genes detected per cell (n_genes_by_counts) and total transcripts detected per cell (total counts) across each of the 19 sSC neuronal types. Data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. f, UMAP embedding of TransA-MERFISH neuron atlas (Fig. 1d), with mWmC+ neurons colored by individual dataset identities corresponding to each reaction (as in panel a). g, UMAP distribution for each of the three datasets separately, showing that all mWmC+ types have contributions from three reactions. e, Stacked barplot shows consistent mWmC+ labeling of each retino-recipient neuron type across datasets, ensuring a stable representation of retino-recipient cell types. h, Bar plots showing the proportions of each cell type across the three replicates. Comparisons across tracing conditions using the Kruskal–Wallis test revealed no differences among cell types (p > 0.05). Data are presented as mean ± SD. i, left, Example of raw MERFISH images with DAPI (gray) and RNA transcripts (blue); colored segmented cell masks are generated using a customized Cellpose 2.0 model. middle, Similar to (left) but overlapped with curated colored masks annotated manually as a benchmark. right, Comparison of Cellpose model-generated masks and curated masks. Light green shows true positive (TP), pink show False Positive (FP), and purple show False Negative (FN). j, Violin plot showing the performance score across three animals. Calculation of precision, recall and F1 are as following: Precision = TP / (TP + FP), Recall = TP / (TP + FN), F1 = 2 * Precision * Recall / (Precision + Recall). The horizontal line within the violin indicates the median. k, Violin plot showing the distribution of Intersection over Union (IoU) across animals and images. Violin plots show the distribution of the data. The centre line indicates the median, and the lower and upper bounds indicate the 25th and 75th percentiles, respectively.

a-e, Consistent dorsal-ventral cluster distribution along the anterior-posterior and medial-lateral axes. Sample images (a) showing the spatial distribution of cell clusters within each slice across the anterior-posterior axis. Compositional distribution of different neuron clusters (b, excitatory; c, inhibitory) across the anterior-to-posterior axis. Compositional distribution of different neuronal clusters (d, excitatory; e, inhibitory) along the medial-to-lateral axis. n = 16 animals. f-g, Sample images showing sublaminar distribution for each ENC (f) or INC (g) along the dorsal-ventral axis of the sSC. The somata median positions along the dorsal-ventral axis are plotted for all ENC and INC (Fig. 1f). Colored lines are the mean; gray lines are individual measurements. Scale bars, 100 μm.

a, Schematic of strategy to examine selective connectivity from all RGCs (AAV2-ChR2-YFP, green) to SC neurons (either SC-FlpO; FSF-RFP or SC-Cre; FSF-RFP, red) using CRACM. b-d, CRACM experiments show findings consistent with those from TransA-MERFISH, in which RGCs innervate ENC5 (Npnt+, b) but not ENC6 (Etv1+, c). Amplitudes of evoked currents and percentages of innervations were quantified in (d). n = 4 animals; 7 out of 13 ENC5 were connected, 2 out of 9 ENC6 were weakly innervated. *p = 0.0478, Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. e-h, Experimental scheme (e) for findings in (Fig. 1k) using immunohistochemistry indicates co-staining with anti-RFP and anti-Npnt antibodies (f,h, n = 4 animals; 128 neurons), whereas no co-localization was observed between goat anti-RFP and rabbit anti-Etv1 antibodies (g,h, n = 4 animals; 103 neurons). (h) Statistical results for f,g. Scale bar, 20 μm. ***p = 0.0004, Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. i, Comparison of the frequencies of labeled Npnt+ wide-field neurons among vGlut2+ neurons within the regions used for MERFISH analysis and replot of the percentage of Npnt+ SC neurons from Liu et al. n = 4 animals. n.s. not significant. Data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. ***p = 0.0002, Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. j-k, Validation of TransA-MERFISH marker gene expression in ENC1 and ENC2 using RNA-Scope in situ hybridization. Cdh7 (red) is enriched in Cdh7-FlpO; FSF-Stop-GFP (Cdh7-GFP, green), indicating correspondence to ENC1 and ENC2 neuron clusters (j), as quantified in (k). Dotted yellow circles indicate in situ signals that overlap with GFP staining. n = 4 biologically independent animals. Scale bars, 50 μm. l-m, Validation of TransA-MERFISH marker gene expression in INC1 using RNA-Scope in situ hybridization. Cbln4 (red) is enriched in Cbln4-FlpO; FSF-Stop-GFP (Cbln4-GFP, green), indicating correspondence to the INC1 neuron cluster (l) as quantified in (m). Dotted yellow circles indicate in situ signals that overlap with GFP staining. n = 4 biologically independent animals. Scale bars: 50 μm. n-o, Validation of TransA-MERFISH marker gene expression in INC1 using RNA-Scope in situ hybridization. Cbln4 expression (red) is exclusive of Cdh7-GFP (green) (n), as quantified in (o). n = 4 biologically independent animals. Scale bars, 50 μm. p-q, Validation of TransA-MERFISH marker gene expression in ENC1 and ENC2 using RNA-Scope in situ hybridization. Itga7 (red, ENC1) and Sntb1 (blue, ENC2) are mutually exclusive in Cdh7-GFP SC neurons (p), as quantified in (q). ENC1 and ENC2 each account for 50% and 25% of the total GFP neurons, respectively, while neither Itga7 nor Sntb1 overlaps. n = 4 biologically independent animals. Scale bars, 50 μm. All data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. Schematics in a,e adapted from ref. 6, Springer Nature.

a, AAV vector design for Pan mWGA-mCherry (AAV2-CAG-mWmC-WPRE) and Cre-dependent mWGA-mCherry (AAV2-CAG-DIO-mWmC-WPRE) expression to achieve neuronal subtype-specific anterograde transsynaptic tracing. RGC percentage is quantified on the right. Scale bar, 20 μm. n = 3 biologically independent animals. b-d, mWGA-mCherry expressed in Foxp2+ RGCs. Foxp2-cre is a driver for the F-RGC subclass (Foxp2-positive, b) but distinct from Spp1, a marker for αRGCs (c), as quantified in (d). n = 3 biologically independent animals e-h, mWGA-mCherry expressed in Tusc5+ RGCs. Tusc5-cre is a driver for the T5-RGC subclass (Tusc5+, (e) but is distinct from Spp1 (f) and partially overlaps with Foxp2 (g), as quantified in (h). n = 4 biologically independent animals i, Normalized GFP axon fluorescence intensity of line scans drawn perpendicular to the SC pia surface (solid line is mean intensity curve; light lines are each example; shadows are s.e.m.) across four different genotypes. Scale bars (b-h), 20μm. n = 5 animals per genotype. All data are presented as mean ± s.e.m. ****, p < 0.001. Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test.

a-e, Cell centroid distribution of each SC cluster along the dorsal-ventral axis labeled with mWmC from all RGCs (a), αRGCs (b), ooDSGCs (c), F-RGCs (d), and T5-RGCs (e), respectively. Each box represents one mWmC+ neuron type annotated via TransA-MERFISH, and the height of each bar represents the distribution of mWmC+ cells along the dorsal-ventral axis annotated via TransA-MERFISH. The side bars indicate the overall distribution of neurons innervated by that RGC type along the dorsal-ventral axis, spanning 0-500 µm from the pial surface (y-axis). Box plots show the center and bounds of the distribution. For (a,b,d,e), n = 3 animals; for (c), n = 4 animals. f, Normalized proportions of mWmC+ cells in retino-recipient neuron types, colored by starter RGC subclass. Bars show the mean fraction of mWmC+ cells per cell type across animals. Normalized fractions were obtained using a hierarchical logistic Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) that accounts for variation across tracing datasets, animals, tissue sections, and cell-type abundance. n = 15 biologically independent animals. Data are presented as mean ± SD.

Sources indicate that a, Sample DIC/fluorescence images from CRACM experiments. Scale bar, 20 µm. b-c, Mapping connectivity from ooDSGCs onto Cdh7+ SC neurons using CRACM. (b) Sample EPSCs in Cdh7+ SC neurons evoked by ooDSGCs (black trace) persist in the presence of bath-applied TTX (1 µM) + 4-AP (100 µM) (blue trace) but are abolished after bath perfusion with CNQX (10 µM) + APV (50 µM) (red trace), indicating a monosynaptic excitatory connection. Blue lines indicate 2 ms period of optogenetic excitation. (c) Quantification of the average amplitudes before and after adding pharmacological blockers in ooDSGC-Cdh7+ SC connected pairs. Current amplitudes before adding any drugs are shown in black dots and bars; blue dots and bars show current amplitude after adding TTX + 4-AP; red dots and bars show current amplitude after adding CNQX + APV. Each dot represents one cell. n = 3 biologically independent animals, 8 cells, n.s. not significant. *, p = 0.0124, Two-sided unpaired Student’s t-test. d-e, CRACM reveals a lack of monosynaptic connections from ooDSGCs onto Cbln4+ SC neurons. (d) Sample ooDSGC-evoked EPSCs have very small amplitudes (black trace) and are blocked by bath-applied TTX (1 µM) + 4-AP (100 µM) (blue trace), indicating that they are polysynaptic. Blue lines indicate 2 ms of blue LED light. (e) Quantification of the average amplitudes before and after adding pharmacological blockers in ooDSGC-Cbln4+ SC tests. Black dots and bars show current amplitudes before adding drugs; blue dots and bars show current amplitudes after adding TTX + 4-AP; red dots and bars show current amplitudes with CNQX + APV. Each dot represents one cell. n = 6 biologically independent animals, 9 cells, **, p = 0.0044, n.s. not significant. Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has no concerns over Calvin Bassey leaving the club in the January transfer window despite interest from Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino has arrived at Old Trafford tasked with lifting the club from their latest malaise and will be backed in January with a defender and a striker needed.

Bassey has emerged as a target at the back with United’s defence in disarray this season, conceding 19 goals in 10 appearances.

Recent findings suggest that bassey’s current contract at Craven Cottage expires in the summer with Fulham holding the option to extend that by a further 12 months. The Cottagers are also in active talks with their captain over a new contract which would effectively put an end to United’s interest.

Fulham have no intention of selling the former Rangers star with Arbeloa describing him as one of the best defenders ‘in the world’.

‘He is one of my captains. From the first days when I arrived I saw how good he is.

‘I think he is one of the best centre backs in the world, so it’s normal if there are so many teams that wants Calvin, that for me is normal.

Sources indicate that ‘I’m not worried about that because I am really happy with Calvin. I think Calvin is really happy here. He is so key for us. He is one of our leaders.’.

Joao Pedro has been ruled out of Chelsea’s Premier League clash with Leeds United this weekend.

The Brazil international has missed his side’s last four games as a result of a thigh injury he suffered in training in October.

The former Brighton star sat out of games against Tottenham, Manchester United, Sunderland and Liverpool in the Carabao Cup with the Blues losing three of those four in his absence.

There was hope he would be available to return after the international break but Xabi Alonso has confirmed his striker is still not ready ahead of the visit of Daniel Farke’s side on Saturday afternoon.

Pedro is still to return to training with his manager unable to put a timeline on his return.

In a recent development, ‘Not yet,’ Alonso noted when asked about his availability. ‘He’s not fit yet to train with the team. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he’s feeling.’.

When asked how confident he is to find a solution in attack in Pedro’s absence, Alonso replied: ’We need the whole team for that.

Sources indicate that ’It’s not just the strikers who can score. We can score from set-pieces, defenders, midfielders, so it’s teamwork, for sure.’He’s an vital player but we need to deal this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’They [Danny Welbeck and Emmanuel Emegha] are both ready, both have different qualities, both at different stages of their career. Danny has played so many games, has great experience, has quality, Emman has this power, this physicality, he’s waiting for his chance and we have enough games to try.’.

Chelsea have other concerns with Maxence Lacroix still sidelined along with Jorrel Hato.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Louis Saha believes Manchester United should have signed Nicolas Jackson before his £65million move from Chelsea to Aston Villa.

Jackson enjoyed a fast start to life at Chelsea, scoring 17 goals in all competitions during his first season at Stamford Bridge.

But the Senegalese striker failed to hit those heights during the 2024-25 campaign and Chelsea sent him on loan to Bayern Munich last season.

The performances of Joao Pedro complicated Jackson’s future upon his return from his loan in Germany, and a sale to Villa was eventually sanctioned, reuniting the 25-year-old with his former Villarreal boss Unai Emery.

Back under Emery’s tutelage, Jackson has returned to his best, with nine goals in 14 appearances so far this season.

And Saha believes United missed a trick by not trying to sign Jackson over the summer, particularly given Benjamin Sesko’s injury woes, which have seen him miss large swathes of this campaign.

‘Nicolas Jackson is a player that I think Man Utd really missed out on because he’s an experienced striker who plays well under pressure,’ Saha told CasinoHawks.

‘Of course, he misses chances sometimes, but his work rate and ability to keep opposing centre-backs busy are vital for team balance.

‘Aston Villa have done really well with those two players, I would’ve loved them at Old Trafford.’.

Saha feels similarly about midfielder Leon Goretzka, who joined Villa on a free transfer from Bayern Munich this summer, with the Frenchman adding: ‘Leon Goretzka was a bargain for Aston Villa.

‘There’s a bit of jealousy seeing someone like Goretzka go to Aston Villa while Man Utd lose Casemiro. You definitely need experienced players in that central area.

According to recent reports, ‘Adapting to the Premier League isn’t always easy, but Villa went for proven quality. It’s frustrating, as those are the types of opportunities Man United should be capitalizing on.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes will remain as Manchester United’s captain, Mauricio Pochettino has confirmed.

The Red Devils’ fresh head coach addressed the media for the first time since his appointment at Old Trafford, as he takes over the reins from Michael Carrick.

United are in the Premier League relegation zone as the Argentine arrives, and he will oversee his new side at Anfield against Liverpool on Sunday in his first game at the helm.

A significant glitch that hangs over the club is the future of captain Fernandes, who has reportedly rejected two offers of a new contract this term.

The Portuguese’s current deal in the north west expires at the end of the current campaign, and come January, he will be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with a foreign club that would see him depart for free.

The No8’s discipline was called into question as well before the international break, when Fernandes called out his former manager’s tactics in the 4-1 demolition by Como in the Champions League.

It led to the Portugal international being benched for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth, but he was immediately reinstated for the 2-0 loss at Chelsea after clear-the-air talks with Carrick.

Now, Pochettino has had his say on the attacking midfielder.

“I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one,” the former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach said.

“Bruno is our captain and he's a very important player, but all the player must feel they are important.

Industry observers note that “We chatted yesterday and spent three hours chatting in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone.”.

The 54-year-old added that there “would be time” to discuss Fernandes’ contract, but refused to be drawn on a straighter answer regarding the skipper’s future.
